kayrasaurus:study:1.title: A new therizinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Jehol Biota and ecomorphological patterns among early therizinosaurians (Journal of Systematic Palaeontology, 2026)

facts.statement: The type locality of Kayrasaurus is the Yixian Formation.
facts.quote: Type locality: Yixian Formation

facts.statement: Kayrasaurus was found in China.
facts.quote: Country: China

facts.statement: Kayrasaurus lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Age: Early Cretaceous

facts.statement: Kayrasaurus was described by Liao and colleagues.
facts.quote: Authors: Liao et al.

facts.statement: Kayrasaurus is a newly described genus and species.
facts.quote: Novelty: Gen. et sp. nov

facts.statement: The taxonomic status of Kayrasaurus is considered valid.
facts.quote: Status: Valid

facts.statement: The genus Kayrasaurus was named by Liao et al. in 2026.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Liao et al., 2026

facts.statement: The only known species of Kayrasaurus is K. changliensis.
facts.quote: species: changliensis

facts.statement: The legs and most of the pelvis of the Kayrasaurus specimen are unknown.
facts.quote: The legs and most of the pelvis are unknown

facts.statement: Kayrasaurus had a length of 3.6 meters and an estimated weight between 117 and 274 kilograms.
facts.quote: With a length of 3.6 m and an estimated weight of 117 - 274 kg

facts.statement: Kayrasaurus is unique among therizinosaurs for having more teeth in its lower jaw than any other species in the group.
facts.quote: It is unique in the small, closely packed teeth in the rest of the upper and lower jaws, bearing more teeth in the mandible than any other therizinosaur

facts.statement: Kayrasaurus possessed notably elongated neck vertebrae and large, strongly curved hand claws.
facts.quote: The vertebrae in the neck are notably elongated, and the claws on the hand are large and strongly curved

facts.statement: The genus Kayrasaurus contains only one species, K. changliensis.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Kayrasaurus changliensis

facts.statement: Kayrasaurus fossils were discovered in the Yixian Formation at Dabangou village near Beipiao in Liaoning Province, China.
facts.quote: The Kayrasaurus fossil material was discovered in outcrops of the Yixian Formation in Dabangou village near Beipiao in Liaoning Province, China

facts.statement: The Kayrasaurus specimen is housed at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology & Paleoanthropology in Beijing.
facts.quote: The specimen is housed at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology & Paleoanthropology (IVPP) in Beijing

facts.statement: The Kayrasaurus specimen is permanently accessioned as IVPP V 18957.
facts.quote: It is permanently accessioned there as specimen IVPP V 18957

facts.statement: Liao Chun-Chi and colleagues described Kayrasaurus changliensis as a new therizinosaurian genus and species in 2026.
facts.quote: In 2026, Liao Chun-Chi and colleagues described Kayrasaurus changliensis as a new genus and species of therizinosaurian dinosaur

facts.statement: The name Kayrasaurus combines 'Kayra', a Turkic shamanism creation god, with the Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: The generic name, Kayrasaurus, combines a reference to Kayra, the creation god in Turkic shamanism, with the Ancient Greek σαῦρος (saûros), meaning lizard

facts.statement: The species name changliensis refers to Changli, a historical name for the region containing the type locality.
facts.quote: The specific name, changliensis, derives from Changli, a historical Three Kingdoms-era name for the region that includes the type locality

facts.statement: Much of the Kayrasaurus skeleton, including the skull and spine, is articulated but compressed by taphonomic deformation.
facts.quote: Much of the skeleton, including the skull and vertebral column, is articulated, albeit compressed via taphonomic deformation

facts.statement: Based on related therizinosaurs, the body mass of Kayrasaurus is estimated at 117 to 274 kilograms.
facts.quote: As such, referencing related therizinosaurs that do have a femur, the body mass of Kayrasaurus can be estimated at 117 - 274 kg

facts.statement: Although the largest therizinosaur from the Jehol Biota, Kayrasaurus was likely not fully grown when it died.
facts.quote: Despite being the largest therizinosaur in the Biota, it was likely not fully grown at the time it died

facts.statement: Open sutures in the neck, trunk, and tail vertebrae suggest the Kayrasaurus specimen was in a subadult stage.
facts.quote: A subadult stage is suggested by the open sutures between the neural arches and centra of the cervical (neck), dorsal (trunk), and first few caudal (tail) vertebrae

facts.statement: CT scans reveal the Kayrasaurus skull is severely flattened and only 3 to 5 millimeters thick.
facts.quote: The skull of the holotype is severely flattened due to taphonomic factors; CT scans of the skull reveal it to be only 3 - 5 mm thick

facts.statement: The Kayrasaurus upper jaw is toothless at the front, with teeth beginning only after the first 28% of the maxilla.
facts.quote: The premaxilla is entirely edentulous (toothless, as in all therizinosauroids), while only the first ~28% of the maxilla lacks teeth

facts.statement: The Kayrasaurus maxilla contains about 32 small, closely packed tooth positions, with 3.5 to 4 per centimeter.
facts.quote: There are about 32 alveoli (tooth positions) in the maxilla, which are very small, shallow, and closely packed, with 3.5 to 4 alveoli per centimetre

facts.statement: Kayrasaurus has a higher lower jaw tooth count than any other therizinosaur, exceeding the counts of Beipiaosaurus, Alxasaurus, and Eshanosaurus.
facts.quote: This indicates a higher mandibular tooth count than any other therizinosaur, as the next closest taxa—Beipiaosaurus, Alxasaurus, and Eshanosaurus—all have fewer than 40

facts.statement: The nasal bone of Kayrasaurus extends further back on the skull than in other therizinosaurs.
facts.quote: The nasal bone, placed on the surface of the snout, extends further toward the back of the skull than in other therizinosaurs

facts.statement: The front end of the Kayrasaurus nasal bone where it meets the premaxilla is two-pronged, a unique feature of the species.
facts.quote: The anterior (front) end of the nasal that meets the premaxilla is two-pronged, another autapomorphy (unique derived feature) of Kayrasaurus

facts.statement: The shape of the external mandibular fenestra is a distinguishing feature of Kayrasaurus.
facts.quote: Another distinguishing feature of this taxon is the shape of the external mandibular fenestra, an opening at the back of the lower jaw

facts.statement: Ten cervical vertebrae of the Kayrasaurus holotype are preserved in natural articulation.
facts.quote: Ten cervical (neck) vertebrae of the holotype are preserved in natural articulation

facts.statement: All Kayrasaurus cervical vertebrae are substantially elongated, with the shortest one longer than the longest dorsal vertebra, a possible unique trait.
facts.quote: These vertebrae are all substantially elongated, with the shortest one still being longer than the longest dorsal (trunk vertebra), a possible autapomorphy of Kayrasaurus

facts.statement: Twelve dorsal vertebrae were likely present in the life of Kayrasaurus, similar to Jianchangosaurus.
facts.quote: Twelve were likely present in life, as in Jianchangosaurus

facts.statement: Unlike the closely related Beipiaosaurus, Kayrasaurus does not have a series of four fused dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: The closely related Beipiaosaurus has a series of four fused dorsal vertebrae, a feature not seen in Kayrasaurus

facts.statement: A nearly complete series of 32 caudal vertebrae is preserved in the Kayrasaurus holotype.
facts.quote: A nearly complete, articulated series of 32 caudal vertebrae is preserved following the sacrum

facts.statement: A decrease in the number of caudal vertebrae is a trend in therizinosaur evolution, as more derived species have fewer than 30.
facts.quote: More derived therizinosaurs have been inferred to have fewer than 30 caudal vertebrae, suggesting that a decrease in the count of these vertebrae is a trend in therizinosaur evolution

facts.statement: Kayrasaurus is an early-diverging member of the Therizinosauria group.
facts.quote: An early-diverging member of the group Therizinosauria

facts.statement: Kayrasaurus is known from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian–Aptian ages) Yixian Formation of China.
facts.quote: known from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian–Aptian ages) Yixian Formation of China

facts.statement: Like other therizinosaurs, the front of the Kayrasaurus jaws were toothless.
facts.quote: Like other therizinosaurs, the front of its jaws were toothless

facts.statement: Kayrasaurus is closely related to the contemporary Beipiaosaurus and Jianchangosaurus.
facts.quote: Kayrasaurus is closely related to the contemporary Beipiaosaurus and Jianchangosaurus, both of which are also known from the Yixian Formation

facts.statement: Most Kayrasaurus teeth were similar in size, though those closest to the front were likely larger.
facts.quote: Most of the teeth of Kayrasaurus would have been similar in size (homodonty), though the alveolar sizes suggest those closest to the front were larger

facts.statement: Kayrasaurus neck vertebrae were pneumatized, indicated by foramina on the lateral surfaces of the centra.
facts.quote: The neural spines are low with rounded upper edges. Foramina are present on the lateral surfaces of the centra, indicating these vertebrae were pneumatised (full of air pockets)

facts.statement: It is debated whether Kayrasaurus reached full adult size, as the specimen was likely a subadult.
facts.quote: Despite being the largest therizinosaur in the Biota, it was likely not fully grown at the time it died

facts.statement: Kayrasaurus possessed a complete furcula with a gracile V-shape typical of therizinosaurs.
facts.quote: The furcula (wishbone) is complete, with a gracile, V-shape typical of therizinosaurs.

facts.statement: The angle between the ends of the furcula in Kayrasaurus was broad at approximately 140 degrees.
facts.quote: The angle between the two ends is broad (~140°), contrasting with the acute angle seen in Falcarius.

facts.statement: The humerus of Kayrasaurus was unusually robust, resembling that of Erliansaurus and Nothronychus graffami.
facts.quote: The humerus is unusually robust, most similar to Erliansaurus and Nothronychus graffami.

facts.statement: The shaft of the humerus in Kayrasaurus was straight, unlike the bowed shaft found in Falcarius.
facts.quote: The shaft of the humerus is straight, unlike the bowed shaft in Falcarius.

facts.statement: The radius of Kayrasaurus was straight and slender, consistent with basal therizinosaurs.
facts.quote: The radius is straight and slender, as in basal therizinosaurs, in contrast to the bowed, robust radii of derived taxa.

facts.statement: The claws of Kayrasaurus were deeply curved with intact distal tips.
facts.quote: The unguals are deeply curved, with their distalmost tips still intact.

facts.statement: The proximal articular end of the first phalanx of digit II in Kayrasaurus was wider than it was high, contrasting with all other therizinosaurs.
facts.quote: The proximal articular end of this phalanx is wider than it is high, contrasting with all other therizinosaurs, in which the opposite is true.

facts.statement: Digit IV was the most gracile manual digit in Kayrasaurus.
facts.quote: Digit IV is the most gracile manual digit.

facts.statement: The iliac blade of Kayrasaurus had a sub-parallelogram shape when viewed from the side, similar to basal therizinosaurs, basal avialans, and dromaeosaurids.
facts.quote: As in basal therizinosaurs, basal avialans, and dromaeosaurids, the iliac blade has a sub-parallelogram shape when seen from the side.

facts.statement: The ischiadic peduncle of Kayrasaurus was peg-like, similar to basal therizinosaurs and distinct from the square-like or circular shape of more derived taxa.
facts.quote: The ischiadic peduncle is peg-like, as in basal therizinosaurs, as opposed to square-like or circular, as in more derived taxa.

facts.statement: The genus Kayrasaurus contains a single species, K. changliensis, named in 2026 based on a nearly complete skeleton including the skull.
facts.quote: El género contiene una sola especie, Kayrasaurus changliensis, nombrada en 2026 basándose en un esqueleto casi completo que incluye el cráneo.

facts.statement: Kayrasaurus is the largest known therizinosaur of the Jehol Biota.
facts.quote: Kayrasaurus es el terizinosaurio más grande conocido de la Biota de Jehol.

facts.statement: Kayrasaurus had a length of 3.6 meters (12 feet) and an estimated weight of 117–274 kilograms (258–604 pounds).
facts.quote: Con una longitud de 3,6 metros (12 pies) y un peso estimado de 117–274 kilogramos (258–604 libras),

facts.statement: Like other therizinosaurs, the front part of Kayrasaurus' jaws lacked teeth.
facts.quote: Al igual que otros terizinosaurios, la parte frontal de sus mandíbulas no tenía dientes.

facts.statement: Kayrasaurus is unique among therizinosaurs for having small, tightly packed teeth in the rest of its upper and lower jaws, and having more teeth in the jaw than any other therizinosaur.
facts.quote: Es único en los dientes pequeños y apretados del resto de las mandíbulas superior e inferior, y tiene más dientes en la mandíbula que cualquier otro terizinosaurio.

facts.statement: The neck vertebrae of Kayrasaurus were notably elongated, and its hand claws were large and strongly curved.
facts.quote: Las vértebras del cuello son notablemente alargadas y las garras de la mano son grandes y fuertemente curvadas.

facts.statement: Fossil material of Kayrasaurus was discovered in outcrops of the Yixian Formation in Dabangou village, near Beipiao, in Liaoning province, China.
facts.quote: El material fósil de Kayrasaurus fue descubierto en afloramientos de la Formación Yixian en la aldea de Dabangou, cerca de Beipiao, en la provincia de Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: The specimen is housed at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology (IVPP) in Beijing, where it was prepared by Ding Xiaoqing.
facts.quote: El espécimen se encuentra en el Instituto de Paleontología y Paleoantropología de Vertebrados (IVPP) en Beijing, donde fue preparado por Ding Xiaoqing.

facts.statement: The specimen is permanently accessible as IVPP V 18957 and consists of a nearly complete skeleton including the skull.
facts.quote: Allí se accede permanentemente como espécimen IVPP V 18957 y consta de un esqueleto casi completo que incluye el cráneo.

facts.statement: Most of the skeleton, including the skull and vertebral column, is articulated but compressed by taphonomic deformation.
facts.quote: Gran parte del esqueleto, incluido el cráneo y la columna vertebral, está articulado, aunque comprimido mediante deformación tafonómica.

facts.statement: The genus Kayrasaurus was described by Liao et al. in 2026.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Liao et al., 2026

facts.statement: The species Kayrasaurus changliensis was described by Liao et al. in 2026.
facts.quote: species_authority: Liao et al., 2026

facts.statement: Kayrasaurus is an extinct genus of therizinosaurian dinosaur known from the Lower Cretaceous Yixian Formation of China.
facts.quote: Kayrasaurus (Lagarto de Kayra) es un género extinto de dinosaurio tericinosaurio conocido de la Formación Yixian del Cretácico Inferior de China.

facts.statement: Kayrasaurus is closely related to the contemporaries Beipiaosaurus and Jianchangosaurus, both also known from the Jehol Biota.
facts.quote: Kayrasaurus está estrechamente relacionado con los contemporáneos Beipiaosaurus y Jianchangosaurus, ambos también conocidos de Jehol.

facts.statement: Kayrasaurus is a medium-sized therizinosaur with a body length of at least 3.6 meters.
facts.quote: Kayrasaurus se considera un terizinosaurio de tamaño mediano, con una longitud corporal de al menos 3,6 metros.

facts.statement: The body mass of Kayrasaurus is estimated to be between 117 and 274 kilograms.
facts.quote: La masa corporal de Kayrasaurus se puede estimar en 117–274 kilogramos (258–604 libras).

facts.statement: Kayrasaurus is substantially larger than Beipiaosaurus, which has an estimated body length of 2.2 meters.
facts.quote: Estas medidas lo hacen sustancialmente más grande que Beipiaosaurus, el siguiente terizinosaurio más grande conocido de la Biota de Jehol, que tiene una longitud corporal estimada de 2,2 m (7,2 ft).

facts.statement: The humerus of Kayrasaurus is unusually robust and similar to those of Erliansaurus and Nothronychus.
facts.quote: El húmero es inusualmente robusto, muy similar al de Erliansaurus y Nothronychus.

facts.statement: The humerus shaft of Kayrasaurus is straight, unlike the arched shaft found in Falcarius.
facts.quote: El eje del húmero es recto, a diferencia del eje arqueado de Falcario.

facts.statement: The radius of Kayrasaurus is straight and slender, resembling basal therizinosaurs, in contrast to the arched and robust radii of derived taxa.
facts.quote: El radio es recto y delgado, como en los terizinosaurios basales, en contraste con los radios arqueados y robustos de los taxones derivados.

facts.statement: The phalanges, including claws, are generally well-preserved in Kayrasaurus with a morphology comparable to Beipiaosaurus.
facts.quote: Las falanges (incluidos los unguales o garras) están generalmente bien conservadas, con una morfología comparable a la de Beipiaosaurus.

facts.statement: The claws of Kayrasaurus are deeply curved with their distal tips still intact.
facts.quote: Los unguales están profundamente curvados, con sus puntas más distales aún intactas.

facts.statement: The claws of Kayrasaurus are similar in length to the penultimate phalanges, resembling basal therizinosaurs but contrasting with the characteristically elongated claws of derived Therizinosaurus and Nothronychus.
facts.quote: Son similares en longitud a las penúltimas falanges, similares a los terizinosaurios basales pero en contraste con los unguales característicamente alargados de los más derivados Therizinosaurus y Nothronychus.

facts.statement: The claw of digit II in Kayrasaurus is smaller than that of digit III, a condition previously thought to be exclusive to Beipiaosaurus.
facts.quote: Es más pequeña que la garra del dedo III, una condición que de otro modo solo se observa en Beipiaosaurus ys que anteriormente se pensaba que esto era exclusivo de ese taxón.

facts.statement: Kayrasaurus belongs to the parent group Therizinosauria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Therizinosauria

facts.statement: Kayrasaurus is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Kayrasaurus lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, from 125.77 to 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)

facts.statement: There is one recorded fossil occurrence of Kayrasaurus in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1
